conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment safety verification gates prevent systemic harm or merely freeze out-of-date biases into permanent institutional concrete while delaying beneficial software updates.

positions.stance: Pre-deployment safety verification prevents unverified diagnostic errors from harming vulnerable patient populations and protects institutional integrity.
Pre-deployment gatekeeping creates multi-year bureaucratic bottlenecks that freeze historical billing-code biases into permanent institutional concrete by blocking algorithmic updates.

conflicts.point: Whether post-deployment runtime telemetry successfully corrects physiological misallocations faster than static boards or merely logs failures after harm has occurred while perpetuating training data contamination.

positions.stance: Deployer-side runtime telemetry combined with pre-programmed safe-state escalation mechanisms catch physiological misallocations faster than any central inspection board.
Post-market telemetry acts as a passive recorder of harm rather than an active barrier against it, logging errors only after incorrect treatment has been administered.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment safety verification prevents systemic harm or merely freezes out-of-date biases into permanent institutional concrete while delaying beneficial software updates.
verdicts.rationale: Both sides present valid empirical risks backed by documented pilot failures and administrative delays, but neither provides comparative longitudinal data proving which approach yields lower net patient harm.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Longitudinal studies comparing patient mortality and resource misallocation rates across jurisdictions with strict pre-market clearance versus those relying solely on post-market telemetry.

verdicts.conflict: Whether post-deployment runtime telemetry successfully corrects physiological misallocations faster than static boards or merely logs failures after harm has occurred while perpetuating training data contamination.
verdicts.rationale: Claim C3 relies on specific 2023 hospital pilot records demonstrating exact failure modes driven by billing-code training, whereas the opposing telemetry claim offers a generalized mechanism without documented remediation timelines.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Audited deployment logs showing that decentralized post-market telemetry successfully identifies and corrects demographic error rates within days rather than years.
